title: Terminar por and Acabar por: How It Ended Up

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *terminar por* and *acabar por* + infinitive from B2 Unit 25: "to end up doing" something after a process. They fit the history of a place at the end of the world, where a prison, a train and a village each ended up as something else.

sections.title: Ending up in Ushuaia
rows: El viejo tren terminó por convertirse en una atracción turística.
after years of use, it ended up as a tourist attraction
El pueblo terminó por crecer alrededor del puerto.
a slow process with a result
La cárcel acabó por cerrarse en 1947.
*acabar por* means the same as *terminar por*
Con el tiempo, acabaremos por conocer la isla.
works in any tense; after *por* always an infinitive

items.spanish: El viejo tren terminó por convertirse en una atracción turística.
items.english: The old train ended up as a tourist attraction.

items.spanish: El pueblo terminó por crecer alrededor del puerto.
items.english: The village ended up growing around the port.

items.spanish: La cárcel acabó por cerrarse en 1947.
items.english: The prison ended up closing in 1947.

items.spanish: Con el tiempo, muchos viajeros acaban por visitar el canal Beagle.
items.english: In time, many travellers end up visiting the Beagle Channel.

sections.content: Use *terminar por* or *acabar por* when there is a process before the result: *el tren terminó por convertirse en…*. Do not confuse *acabar por* with *acabar de*, which means "to have just done" something. After *por* the verb is always an infinitive.
